lesson.title: Saturday Point #2
lesson.hook: A return game at 5–2, built from five of your lessons. Two choices each shot: the one you want to hit, and the one that wins.
lesson.memHTML: Return deep. Keep the depth. Finish at the net.
lesson.tomorrow: In your next match, when you're ahead, check that your balls aren't getting shorter. Keep them deep.

steps.name: Their big serve
steps.sit: You lead 5–2. Their serve: a big first serve, wide to your forehand.
steps.payoff: Deep through the middle takes the angle away from their next ball.
steps.principle: Against a big serve, deep through the middle takes their weapon away.
steps.why: Off their best serve, the sideline is a low-percentage target and it goes wide. Deep through the middle gives them no angle for their +1.
steps.take: Big serve coming? Deep through the middle.

lines.A: Right: deep through the middle. Their +1 has no angle.
lines.B: Going for the line off their best serve: wide.

steps.name: Keep the depth
steps.sit: Their +1 pushes you into your backhand corner.
steps.payoff: The depth that built the lead keeps them back.
steps.principle: Ahead? Keep the depth that built the lead.
steps.why: Leading makes the safe, shorter ball feel smart, but it lets them step in and take over. Deep crosscourt keeps them where they've been all set.

lines.A: Shorter lets them step in and take over. You're stretched.
lines.B: Right: deep crosscourt keeps them back and pulls them wide.

steps.name: Where to go
steps.sit: Your deep crosscourt pulls them wide.
steps.payoff: Your shot moved their best reply, so the middle moved too.
steps.principle: Recover to their angles, not the centre mark.
steps.why: Pulled wide, their percentage reply is crosscourt. Shading toward it gets you there in time to change direction; the centre mark leaves you stretched.
steps.take: Pulled them wide? Shade toward their crosscourt.

lines.A: Right: in time for their crosscourt, and you change direction.
lines.B: The centre leaves their crosscourt open. You're stretched.

steps.name: Their short slice
steps.sit: Stretched again, they can only slice it back short.
steps.payoff: A deep approach keeps them back and builds a high volley.
steps.principle: A deep approach builds an easy volley.
steps.why: A short approach gives them time and a target for the pass. Deep keeps them behind the baseline, and their pass comes to you higher and slower.

lines.A: Short gives them time and a target. Passed.
lines.B: Right: deep keeps them back. Close in.

steps.name: Their pass
steps.sit: You're closing in. They're winding up for the pass.
steps.q: When should your split step land?
opts: Early, so you're ready and waiting
steps.payoff: Landing as they hit lets you push the moment the pass appears.
steps.principle: Land for their hit, not before it or after it.
steps.why: Land as they hit and you push off the moment the pass can be read: 0.21 s to spare at the volley. Land early and you settle, then push late: 0.09 s, less than half the time.
steps.take: At the net? Land your split as they hit.

lines.A: Right: you push as the pass appears. Set, and you put it away.
lines.B: Early, you settle and push late: 0.09 s to spare instead of 0.21.
